issues.evidence: probes/A_raw.json build log: 'i686-elf-ld: warning: build/kernel.elf has a LOAD segment with RWX permissions'
issues.summary: Linker script merges text/data into one RWX segment, producing a build warning.

issues.evidence: ls A/build (os.img, *.o, kernel.elf checked into the working tree)
issues.summary: Build artifacts are shipped alongside sources.
Sector-count computation relies on BSD stat flags, so the build is not portable to GNU coreutils hosts.

issues.evidence: B/boot.asm int 13h AH=42h with no AH=41h check; booting B/os.img with -boot a -drive if=floppy prints 'Disk read error'
issues.summary: Bootloader assumes BIOS LBA extensions and has no CHS fallback, so it only boots as a hard disk image.

issues.evidence: ls B (os.img, boot.bin, kernel.bin, *.o in source dir); Makefile has no .PHONY
issues.summary: Build artifacts mixed with sources and phony targets undeclared.

blinding_guess.why: A has a structured layout, a size guard in the Makefile and a unittest suite with a headless QEMU boot check, typical of a spec/test-driven process.

notes: Both images build from clean, boot in QEMU into 32-bit protected mode, write kernel text to VGA 0xB8000, and stay up for 10s with -no-reboot; each was booted with its own documented drive type (A floppy, B IDE disk). B also adds a polled-keyboard shell (verified by sending 'help' through the QEMU monitor), which is extra but harmless. A's 5 own tests pass; B ships no tests. Static reports: A's bandit/ruff findings are low-severity subprocess/style notes in its test file only; B has no Python. Neither side has a security-relevant attack surface.
